open_points.subject: 01_models.md Status vs binding force
open_points.question: Is State 1 normative and binding for downstream states/code now, or still provisional so later writers may change model facts silently?
options: State 1 is accepted and binding despite the word "Draft"
State 1 is not yet accepted; later states may revise model facts
open_points.default_guess: Treat State 1 as binding because it is the only available model source.

open_points.subject: M05 Implementation read access (inspect vs K-12)
open_points.text: State 0 primary action: "inspect functions, flows, runs, bindings, approvals, standing grants and effect attempts | owner, agent"; K-12: "For repair an agent receives one contract, its current implementation and that slot's recent traces and trial evidence; for composition, contracts, bindings and not implementation bodies."
open_points.question: Under which exact product actions and permissions may an agent read implementation code bodies?
options: Any agent may inspect any implementation body
Only may-author agents may read implementation bodies
Agents may read implementation bodies only in a slot-scoped repair path, not general inspect
open_points.default_guess: Allow code-body reads only in the slot-scoped repair context (K-12), not broad inspect.

open_points.subject: M25 StandingGrant applicability to draft-write nodes
open_points.text: Grant action: "a `destructive` node or a version that is not active cannot be granted"; K-08 runtime stop rule names only "`state-transition`, `external-effect` and `destructive`"; M26 authority says draft-write uses flow activation (except resend after `not_applied`).
open_points.question: Can a standing grant be created for a `draft-write` node, and if so does it have any effect?
options: Allow grant for draft-write nodes but it is operationally inert
Allow grant and use it as authority for draft-write sends
open_points.default_guess: Allow but inert (record exists, send authority remains flow activation except fresh-approval resend case).

open_points.subject: Run end semantics on owner refusal with concurrent work
open_points.text: "a refusal ends the run `refused`" and "While some nodes wait, independent branches keep running (K-09)."
open_points.question: When owner refusal occurs, what happens to other branches already running or ready to run in the same run?
options: Immediate global stop: schedule nothing further and terminate run
Let already-running local work finish, but start nothing new
Allow all independent work to continue despite run status becoming refused
open_points.default_guess: Immediate global stop with no further node starts once refusal is decided.

open_points.subject: Run cancellation semantics for in-flight execution
open_points.text: Cancel action output: "the run ends `cancelled`; nothing further is sent".
open_points.question: At cancellation time, how are in-flight operation attempts and currently executing function sandboxes represented in model facts/traces?
options: Mark run cancelled immediately; keep existing attempt records as-is and do not start new sends
Wait for in-flight attempts/sandboxes to conclude before final run cancellation
Force-stop in-flight work and emit synthetic terminal node/attempt statuses
open_points.default_guess: Mark run cancelled immediately, prevent new sends, and preserve already-recorded in-flight facts without synthetic remapping.

open_points.subject: M26 authority reference to flow activation identity
open_points.text: M26 authority: "for a `draft-write` send the flow activation under which the run started"; M19 stores `flow_version_id` but no explicit `flow_activation_id` pin.
open_points.question: Is the exact FlowActivation entity identity part of run-pinned facts, or inferred later from timing/order?
options: Run must pin and store the exact `flow_activation_id`
Run stores only flow_version and authority infers activation by latest-before-start order
Authority should reference flow version, not activation entity
open_points.default_guess: Infer from store order at run start (latest activation before run start), since no explicit run field is defined.
